summary: Created scripts/read-log.js — standalone CJS Node.js log reader with zero external dependencies.
Text output format: HH:MM:SS [stage] WP-NNN action → result (duration, tokens) with ANSI color coded by log level.
Summary mode extracts run timestamps, duration, WP counts, token totals, error/warning counts all on one line.
Registered read-log command in scripts/cli.js under Orchestrator category (key: l) with matching printHelp() entry.
All 10 acceptance criteria verified against live orchestrator log files.

comments.note: scripts/read-log.js: The --format json output uses JSON.stringify with 2-space indent (pretty-printed). For large log files piped to other tools, a --compact flag could reduce output size. Low priority since current usage is human-plus-tool readable.

scripts/cli.js: printHelp() uses a hardcoded rows array that must be manually kept in sync with COMMANDS. A future improvement could auto-generate the help rows from the COMMANDS registry to eliminate this dual-maintenance.

scripts/read-log.js: The --last default of 20 (applied only when no other filter is active) differs slightly from typical CLI conventions where --last would always apply. The current behavior (documented in help) is intentional per spec but may surprise users who combine --actions with --last expecting the default 20 to still apply.

summary: All 10 acceptance criteria verified and pass. scripts/read-log.js is a correct, zero-dependency CJS Node.js implementation. Node.js syntax check passes. MCP server test suite (1738 tests, 58 files) passes with no regressions. Edge cases validated: malformed JSON skipped silently, empty log file handled gracefully (exit 0, no crash), nonexistent slug exits 1 with clear message, --file with nonexistent path exits 1. Default 20-entry limit applies only when no other filter is active — verified correct. CLI delegation via node scripts/cli.js read-log works correctly.

comments.note: scripts/cli.js was modified as part of WP-001 (not WP-004's formal scope), pre-registering both read-log and kill-orchestrator commands. All changes work correctly. WP-004 likely needs only validation, not new implementation — the Developer should verify this when WP-004 unblocks.

--summary combined with --format json outputs plain text summary, not a JSON object. The spec does not define --summary JSON behavior, so this is acceptable. The current behavior avoids ambiguity and is consistent with --summary being a dedicated single-line display mode.

Empty log file (all blank/whitespace lines) exits 0 with '(no entries match the filter)' rather than exit 1. Per spec, exit 1 is only for file-not-found or no-logs-in-directory — an empty file is a valid file. Behavior is correct.

summary: PASS — implementation is well-architected, zero-dependency, and fully cross-platform. Two Fix-Forward corrections applied directly.

Fix 1: Inverted condition in parseArgs default case (scripts/read-log.js). `if (eq !== -1) i--;` was logically backwards: when eq===-1 the value was consumed via argv[++i] and i needs to be restored; when eq!==-1 i was never incremented so decrementing causes an infinite loop on any unrecognised --flag=val argument. Fixed to `if (eq === -1) i--;` to match the stated intent in the comment.

Fix 2: Dead code in formatEntry (scripts/read-log.js). `parts.push(result ? arrow : '')` inside `if (result) { ... }` — the inner ternary always evaluates to arrow because the outer conditional already guarantees result is truthy. Simplified to `parts.push(arrow)`.
scripts/cli.js additions (cmdReadLog, cmdKillOrchestrator, COMMANDS entries, printHelp rows) are correct, consistent with existing patterns, and properly scoped.
All 10 acceptance criteria remain met. QA validation is fully intact — both fixes are non-behavioral for all specified inputs.

comments.note: scripts/read-log.js parseArgs() default case: condition `if (eq !== -1) i--;` was inverted. For the `--flag val` form (eq===-1), argv[++i] consumed the next element and that increment must be undone with i--. For the `--flag=val` form (eq!==-1), i was never incremented, so decrementing causes an infinite reprocessing loop. Fixed to `if (eq === -1) i--;`. Comment updated to match.

scripts/read-log.js formatEntry(): `parts.push(result ? arrow : '')` is dead code — the enclosing `if (result)` already guarantees result is truthy, so the ternary is always arrow. Simplified to `parts.push(arrow)` to remove the redundancy.

scripts/read-log.js parseArgs(): unrecognised flags in `--flag val` form (eq===-1, now correctly handled) silently consume the trailing value. A future improvement could check whether the next token starts with `--` before consuming it, which would prevent accidental swallowing of the following flag when the unknown flag takes no argument. Low priority since the script's flag set is stable and well-documented.
